meta.description: Turns untargeted LC-MS/MS features (m/z, RT, MS/MS) into confidence-stratified metabolite annotations using spectral-library matching (matchms), in-silico tools (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID, MetFrag) and molecular networking, and assigns a defensible MSI/Schymanski confidence level.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 13 cited references (Sumner 2007, Schymanski 2014, Li 2021, Duhrkop 2019/2021, Hoffmann 2022, Ruttkies 2016, Wang 2016, Nothias 2020, Kind & Fiehn 2006, Zhou 2020, Theodoridis 2023, Huber 2020) are real, verifiable papers whose cited claims (thresholds, taxonomy) match their actual content; no fabricated statistics or invented values appeared in any of the 5 executed/inspected outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Chemical/analytical annotation only; no output makes a diagnostic, prescriptive, or individual-patient claim, so no medical disclaimer is required for this scope.

methodological_ground.detail: No output substituted correlation for causation or inverted a conclusion; the Skill actively and correctly warns against treating a cosine score as identity (Input 1) and against claiming a specific isomer MS/MS cannot resolve (Inputs 3, 5).

code_usability.detail: All executed code (Inputs 1, 3, 4, 5) ran to completion after documented adaptation; Input 2 (SIRIUS) was not executed due to an external login gate (TOOLS.md), not an unrunnable-code failure, so it does not trigger this dimension.

functional_suitability.note: Library matching (matchms) and confidence-level assignment are fully worked with code; MetFrag is named as one of three annotation routes but has zero executable guidance (no parameter-file skeleton, unlike SIRIUS's full bash block) -- verified gap, see Input 3.

reliability.note: Common Errors table is thorough (7 documented failure modes) but one entry is factually wrong for the Skill's own stated-compatible matchms 0.33+: missing precursor_mz raises AssertionError, not 'scores all zero' -- verified two independent ways in Input 1.

performance_context.note: Single ~220-line SKILL.md, usage-guide.md and one example script; no bloat, no unused content loaded upfront.

agent_usability.note: Decision-tree table (evidence -> tool -> achievable level) and Per-Method Failure Modes section give an agent a cold-start-usable, consistently-labeled workflow with explicit output expectations at each step.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language and realistic example prompts; forgiveness is solid for matchms errors (Common Errors table) but absent for MetFrag, where an agent has no documented recovery path at all.

security.note: SIRIUS login uses an env-var pattern ($SIRIUS_USER), never a hardcoded credential; no injection vectors in any code pattern.

maintainability.note: Clean single-file sectioning and explicit version-compatibility guidance (introspect on ImportError/AttributeError/TypeError) aid modifiability; only one runnable example ships, no test harness.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description, correct progressive disclosure (SKILL.md/usage-guide/examples), bidirectional Related-Skills cross-references, fully deterministic logic (confirmed by re-running), and explicit escape hatches ('MS alone insufficient', 'demand a standard').

inputs.label: matchms library match with score+peak floor on synthetic MS/MS
inputs.note: 3/4 synthetic queries resolved correctly (clean 2a match, promiscuous few-peak rejection, weak/no-hit rejection); the 4th (no precursor_mz) crashed with AssertionError, contradicting SKILL.md's own Common Errors table which claims a silent zero score for this exact case -- verified two independent ways.

assertions.text: Output states an explicit MSI/Schymanski confidence level, not a bare compound name
assertions.note: Every resolved query printed a level (2a or 5).

assertions.text: Matched-peak floor is enforced alongside the cosine score, not score alone
assertions.note: Q2 correctly demoted to Level 5 despite score 0.832 because only 2 of the required 6 peaks matched.

assertions.text: Missing-precursor_mz failure mode matches the Skill's own Common Errors table
assertions.note: Table claims 'scores all zero'; actual matchms 0.33.1 behavior is a hard AssertionError, confirmed via the full run and an isolated .pair() call.

assertions.text: Code uses matchms's documented version-safe field lookup (dtype.names) rather than hardcoded field names
assertions.note: Ran correctly against matchms 0.33.1's class-prefixed field names (e.g. ModifiedCosineGreedy_score).

inputs.label: SIRIUS formula/fingerprint/structure/CANOPUS chain on a library-absent feature
inputs.note: Not executed: SIRIUS 6 requires a free-account login (sirius login) with no anonymous CLI path, blocked in this audit env per TOOLS.md. Command syntax and version caveats (v5/v6 plural subcommand change, COSMIC FDR requirement) were inspected only, not run.

assertions.text: Documents that SIRIUS requires an account/login before use
assertions.note: Explicit comment and 'sirius login' step precede the pipeline.

assertions.text: Distinguishes formula (trustworthy) from top-1 structure (needs COSMIC FDR) rather than treating all SIRIUS outputs as equally confident
Command syntax was verified against a running SIRIUS installation
assertions.note: Blocked by login gate; not executed in this audit, per TOOLS.md.

inputs.label: MetFrag structure ranking for a feature with no library spectrum
inputs.note: Ran successfully and independently reproduced the Skill's own 'isomer wall' claim (citrate/isocitrate tied at score 1.0, glucose correctly discriminated at 0.12) -- but only after building the entire MetFrag parameter file and candidate CSV from outside knowledge, since SKILL.md gives zero executable guidance for this named tool.

assertions.text: Output distinguishes tied isomer candidates rather than reporting a single confident structure
assertions.note: Citrate and isocitrate both scored 1.0 (4/6 peaks explained each).

assertions.text: SKILL.md supplies a runnable MetFrag invocation pattern comparable to its SIRIUS bash block
assertions.note: Verified absent: no parameter-file skeleton or CLI line for MetFrag anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.

assertions.text: MetFrag score is treated as a fragment-support ranking, not an identification
assertions.note: Consistent with the Skill's own Tool Roles table description.

assertions.text: Tool failure on bad input surfaces a clear, non-silent error
assertions.note: MetFrag's own 'Parameter file is missing!' and '0 candidate(s) stored' messages are loud and diagnosable.

inputs.label: MS1-only accurate mass + isotope pattern, no MS/MS
inputs.note: SKILL.md's assign_level() snippet ran unmodified and returned Level 4 for a clean unambiguous formula, Level 5 otherwise, matching the decision-tree table exactly.

assertions.text: Function returns Level 4 only when formula is unambiguous, never higher without structural/library evidence
Bare/ambiguous MS1 feature is not over-promoted to a named compound
assertions.note: Ambiguous-adduct and bare-feature cases both correctly returned Level 5.

assertions.text: Output ties the returned level to the specific evidence key that triggered it
assertions.note: Code path maps each evidence dict key directly to a level, no black box.

inputs.label: 6-feature end-to-end pipeline with pathway-safety flagging
inputs.note: All 6 synthetic features (library-matched, promiscuous, no-hit, MS1-only, bare) correctly leveled and flagged for pathway safety per the Skill's 'database-mapping inflation' warning; the synthetic isomer pair built for this run did not happen to tie under matchms scoring, so the tied-candidate code path itself was not exercised here (it was exercised via MetFrag in Input 3).

assertions.text: Every feature's output includes an explicit confidence level, never a bare name
Ambiguous/tied or unmatched features are flagged as unsafe for pathway enrichment, not silently passed through
assertions.note: F2, F4, F5, F6 all flagged NO.

assertions.text: Isomer/tied-candidate handling degrades to Level 3 rather than picking an arbitrary single winner
assertions.note: Code path exists but this run's synthetic isomer pair did not score as tied, so the path was not actually exercised/verified here.

assertions.text: MS1-only features are capped at Level 4, never promoted with only isotope/mass evidence

key_strengths: Per-Method Failure Modes and quantitative-threshold tables translate directly into working, verifiable code (score+matched-peak floor, decision-tree level assignment), confirmed correct across 4 independently executed inputs.

The MSI/Schymanski confidence-level framing is rigorously sourced (Sumner 2007, Schymanski 2014, Theodoridis 2023) and consistently enforced end to end, including flagging ambiguous annotations before they reach pathway enrichment.
Version-compatibility guidance (ModifiedCosineGreedy rename, dtype-derived field names) is verified correct against the installed matchms 0.33.1, unlike Skills that hardcode brittle field names.
Independently reproduced the Skill's own 'isomer wall' claim via a real MetFrag run: citrate and isocitrate tied at score 1.0 while an unrelated sugar scored 0.12.

recommendations.title: Common Errors table misdescribes the missing-precursor_mz failure
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md states ModifiedCosine 'silently returns zeros' when precursor_mz is missing; matchms 0.33.1 (the version the Skill itself declares compatible) instead raises a hard AssertionError, verified two independent ways.
recommendations.root_cause: The Common Errors table was not re-verified against the matchms 0.33+ release the Skill claims compatibility with.
recommendations.fix: Change the table row to 'raises AssertionError: Precursor_mz missing' for matchms 0.33+, and add AssertionError to the version-note's list of exceptions an agent should catch and introspect.

recommendations.title: MetFrag has zero executable guidance despite being a named route
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md list MetFrag as one of three annotation routes (also in the frontmatter description) but supply no parameter-file skeleton, database-mode guidance, or CLI line, unlike SIRIUS's full bash block. The audit had to hand-build a parameter file and candidate CSV from outside knowledge to get a working run.
recommendations.root_cause: The SIRIUS section was fleshed out with a worked example; MetFrag was left at the tool-roles-table mention level.
recommendations.fix: Add a MetFrag section mirroring the SIRIUS one: a minimal params.txt template (PeakListPath, MetFragDatabaseType, LocalDatabasePath or PubChem, FragmentPeakMatchAbsoluteMassDeviation, MetFragCandidateWriter) plus one CLI invocation line.

recommendations.title: matchms code path can never surface a tied library match
recommendations.problem: The isomer-wall warning is prose-only for the matchms route; the only worked code (`max(pairs, key=...)`) extracts a single best hit by construction, so an agent following the Skill's own pattern cannot detect a tie the way the prose warns about.
recommendations.root_cause: The library-matching code block was written for the single-winner case only; tie detection was never added even though the Skill explicitly discusses the isomer wall.
recommendations.fix: Extend the library-matching example to keep all hits within a small score margin of the top hit (not just the argmax) and report a candidate set, matching the guidance already given for MetFrag/SIRIUS candidate sets.

recommendations.title: Example script comment describes the wrong rejection reason
recommendations.problem: examples/annotate_features.py's docstring says query_promiscuous 'scores high on too few peaks,' but the measured score (0.69) is already below the 0.7 score floor, so Level 5 is reached via the score floor, not the matched-peak floor as the comment implies.
recommendations.root_cause: The synthetic intensities were not tuned to actually clear the score floor before hitting the peak floor.
recommendations.fix: Adjust the query_promiscuous intensities so its score clears 0.7, isolating the matched-peak floor as the actual rejection reason the comment describes.

recommendations.title: Shipped example has no self-check
recommendations.problem: annotate_features.py prints its result but asserts nothing, so a future matchms version bump could silently change the output without failing.
recommendations.root_cause: No regression assertion was included in the only shipped runnable example.
recommendations.fix: Add `assert level == '2a'` (and similar) lines to annotate_features.py so it doubles as a regression check.
